newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-GUATEMALA BEATS COSTA RICA IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GUATEMALA BEATS COSTA RICA IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: Guatemala kept alive its World Cup hopes Sunday, beating arch-rival Costa Rica 1-0 in a CONCACAF group A qualifying match in Los Angeles.
The only goal of the game came in the 34th minute when Guatemala's Juan Plata struck home a penalty after Costa Rican defender Vladimir Quesada was judged to have handled the ball.

The win opened up the race to join the United States in the semifinal round to decide the three teams from the North, Central America and Caribbean region that will advance to the World Cup finals in France 1998.

The United States earlier won its third successive qualifying match 1-0 against Trinidad and Tobago in Port of Spain. The Americans have nine points from three games, Costa Rica has six and Guatemala has four after Sunday's match.

The Guatemala-Costa Rica matchup had been scheduled to be played in Guatemala City on October 16, but the game was abandoned before the start when 84 fans were crushed to death in a stampede at the stadium.
The Guatemalan players were wearing black armbands at the Los Angeles Coliseum Sunday and there was a minute's silence before the kickoff in remembrance of the fans who died.

As a result of the stampede, FIFA ordered Guatemala to play all its home qualifiying games away -- in Los Angeles on Sunday and also on December 8 against Trinidad and Tobago and on December 21 versus the United States in neutral El Salvador.
The United States Soccer Federation has pledged to donate $25,000 to the disaster relief effort.
Guatemala, which had played a physical game losing 2-0 to the Americans in Washington on November 3, came out hard Sunday against their Central American rivals who had beaten them 3-0 in Costa Rica.
Plata's header was pushed around the post by Costa Rican goalkeeper Hermidio Barrantes in the 26th minute and twice Julio Rodas went close before the Guatemalans scored.

Left-back Martin Machon overlapped on the left wing and when he hit a hard cross into the centre, the ball appeared to hit off Quesada's head and bounce away for a corner. However Salvadoran referee Rafael Rodriguez pointed straight to the spot and Plata blasted the ball high past Barrantes.

On the stroke of halftime Barrantes saved Costa Rica from going two-down when he parried Jorge Rodas' 20-yard free kick. The ball fell to Rodas' brother Julio, but Barrantes pushed his header round the post.

Costa Rica never really threatened and Julio Rodas should have put Guatemala further ahead in the 79th minute when he broke in alone on Barrantes on a breakaway, but his sharp shot was well parried by the keeper.
The closest Costa Rica came to equalising was in the 80th minute when Guatemalan goalkeeper Edgar Estrada dived full length to push Austin Berry's 20-yard left-foot volley round the post.

Guatemala: Edgar Estrada, Martin Machon, Eduardo Acevedo, Erik Miranda, Julio Giron, German Ruano, Julio Rodas, Jorge Rodas, Juan Plata (Rocael Quintana, 75th minute),Manuel Funes (Raul Calderon 81st), Everaldo Valencia (Carlos Lemus 60th).

Costa Rica - Hermidio Barrantes, Vladimir Quesada (Oscar Ramirez 68th), Javier Delgado, Luis Marin, Jose Pablo Fonseca (Austin Berry 46th minute), Alex Madrigal, Mauricio Wright (Paulo Wanchope, 46th), Mauricio Solis, Wilmer Lopez, Rolando Fonseca, Ronald Gomez.
